replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: To solve a second order algebraic equation, first, you need to write it in the standard form ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, you can use the quadratic formula x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a) to find the roots. You can also use factoring or completing the square methods. Once you have the roots, you can substitute them back into the equation to verify your solutions.

To find the stationary points of an equation y = f(x), you first need to find the derivative of the function, f'(x). Then, set the derivative equal to zero and solve for x. These solutions are the x-coordinates of the stationary points. To find the y-coordinates, substitute these x-values back into the original function y = f(x). Finally, you can use the second derivative test to determine whether these points are maxima, minima, or points of inflection.
